New location in Thao Dien is of the best Vietnamese restaurants in HCMC.
Jan 2023
The newly opened SH Garden in Thao Dien uses a traditional cooking style, similar to Cuc Gach Quan or TIB, rather than trying to reinvent Vietnamese foods with a modern twist. Personally, I strongly prefer Vietnamese food in traditional styles. Hence, SH Garden is one of my top 3 picks for Vietnamese restaurants in HCMC, along with Cuc Gach Quan and TIB.

They also have an extensive menu of vegetables dishes, making it a great choice for vegetarians and people who want to eat healthily.

The food was delicious, and I highly recommend it.

The interior is spacious and relaxing, with extensive use of wood. And service was attentive.

Overall, I think its much better than the other Vietnamese restaurants in Thao Dien. 

My only request is that they add some local craft beer to the menu, especially an IPA such as Pasteur Street’s Jasmine IPA.

A gem for Vietnamese cuisines
Nov 2022
I dined in SH garden with a friend on our first night in HCMC, and because it was such a rush we left somewhat still intrigued and felt like we needed to try again. On the first occasion we ordered the pomelo salad, fried tiny anabas and we wanted to order the stir fried clams which was sold out, so we changed to the stewed chicken with lemongrass. Of the three, we thought that the chicken was ordinary but we really enjoyed the other two dishes.

Then the second time we went, we ordered the Coconut Meat Salad with Tiger Prawn and Squid which was sublime, a classic note of Vietnam (spicy, sweet, tangy with the umami touch from the fish sauce). The second dish that we ordered was the Stir Fried Clams with Lemon Grass and Grilled Rice Paper (this time its still available...yay), and it was not disappoint. And then come our last dish which was appropriately the pinnacle of our dining experience there: the Grilled Beef with Fish Sauce Wrapped in Mustard Greens and served with soy sauce and wasabi with some pound birds eye chilly on the side. It was an explosion of tastes in our mouth, different flavours (bitter, spicy, savory) that I thought would never work together, yet in this dish they form a brilliant combo that hit your palate with such a gusto.
